Which home address should the employee give: the current one, or the one that applies from the first working day? A new hire who is moving from abroad to Switzerland, or the other way, gets a different source tax liability, canton, cross-border questions and tariff code depending on which address counts. The spec treats the home address country as the country of residence without saying for which date.

Does the questionnaire start empty, or does it show the first working day HR already agreed, for the employee to confirm or correct? HR says 'I ask them to confirm it', which suggests HR already has a date. The spec only says the employee 'enters' it. This decides whether HR provides a value that is shown at the start.

Should the employee ever see the derived results (insurance start date, civil status as the fund will receive it, whether they are subject to source tax, the tariff code or the Liechtenstein result), for example before submitting or in the read-only view? Or are these recorded only for HR? The spec says 'recorded for HR' but never says what the employee sees.

For Liechtenstein residents with more than 45 non-return days, the calculator gives the normal tariff code together with 'Unter Vorbehalt des Doppelbesteuerungsabkommens' (subject to the double taxation agreement) (F-zh_source_tax_calculator-ab4e1e, C1Y / Unter Vorbehalt…). The spec records only the normal tariff code and flags only the 'no liability' case. Should the 'subject to the double taxation agreement' note and the HR flag also go with the tariff code in this case?

Liechtenstein residents who return daily, or expect at most 45 non-return days, get no tariff code. Yet they are asked the denomination, whether the spouse works, and all the children questions before the cross-border step, and none of those answers is used. Is that intended, given data minimisation (G-01)? Or should the cross-border questions come first for Liechtenstein residents so the tariff questions can be skipped, and should those answers be discarded on submission?

Child result row 22, and AC-06.4.3 with it: a minor child of a non-married employee who does NOT live in the household (parental custody, alternating care, employee pays more) 'counts with H'. The calculator note F-zh_source_tax_calculator-96658b says a child counts with H only when it lives in the household. Which is right: H or counted without H (A)? The answer changes the tariff letter.

The house number is required for every employee, but the notes say the sources do not cover addresses without one (rural addresses, building names, some foreign addresses). Can the employee submit without a house number, and if so how? As written, these employees cannot submit at all.

"Step 7 'Children' – one block per child, repeated for each child the employee adds; all child_* conditions refer to the same child." - 'child_*' is an internal field-id prefix used in prose. Business readers should not see identifier naming.
"Afterwards Step 9 'Finish': permit reminder (rule permit_reminder), then submission" - Uses an internal rule id ('permit_reminder') in prose instead of the business name of the rule.

"When Lonio has decided whether the employee is subject to source tax (rule subject_to_source_tax)" - Uses an internal rule identifier in an acceptance criterion. That is an implementation artifact, not business language.

"(The formal expression covers one child block; the digit is the sum over all children.)" - Refers to how the rule is encoded (a 'formal expression' per child block). That is an implementation detail of the rule engine, not a business statement.

"the employee goes through one block of questions per child and can add another child or remove one" - Prescribes the interaction (repeatable blocks with add and remove controls, copied from the calculator UI). The need is only to capture each child's answers.

"their answers are kept, so that if the employee changes the earlier answer back, the earlier input reappears and need not be entered again" - Turns D-036's permissive 'may be kept' into required draft-retention and re-display behaviour, which is an implementation choice.

info.message: If the employee answers 'yes' to having children, must they add at least one child block before they can submit? And is there a maximum number of children? Today an employee could say 'yes' and add no child at all.

D-036 says inapplicable answers 'may be kept' until submission. AC-08.2.1 says they are kept and reappear when the earlier answer is changed back. Is keeping them a requirement or only allowed? Does it also apply if the employee leaves and comes back later in a new session, before submitting?

What are the valid ranges for dates? For example: can the first working day be in the past or far in the future, and must the date of birth (employee and spouse) be in the past or show a minimum age? Without this there are no rejection criteria to test.
The 60-day (Germany) and 45-day (Liechtenstein) questions refer to the calendar year. For someone who starts mid-year, does the employee estimate for the rest of the current year or for a full year?

Which countries can be chosen for the home address, the nationality and the spouse's residence and nationality? Is there an option for stateless people or an unknown nationality? And which of several non-Swiss nationalities should the employee enter?

Some example tables use the same item as both input and expected output (AC-08.4.2 lists 'Nationality' twice; AC-05.4.3 has 'Spouse / partner is gainfully employed…' as input and output 'asked'). Which value is the expected result, so the examples can be tested?

uncited_units.text: HR meeting transcript Everyone and everything here is fictional. Anna is the HR manager at Muster AG. Leo works in product at Lonio.
Can you hear me okay? You're a bit quiet.
Is this better? I'm in the small meeting room, the big one is taken. Sorry, let me just close the door.
Much better. So, thanks for making the time. The idea today is simple. We want your new employees to give us everything once, so that you stop chasing them for
Yes, please. Right now it's a mess. I have a Word document, then an Excel file, and then I type everything into the portals by hand. Last month I spent a full a
Okay. And how many people do you hire in a year?
Around twenty. More in summer. We're about a hundred and fifty people now, mostly here in Zurich.
Good. Let's start with the biggest pain. What takes you the most time?
Okay, that's clear. And the questionnaire itself is what?
Great. Do you also want a photo? Some customers ask for one.
It could. Do you want that from day one?
We're with Pensionskasse Muster. They have a portal, it's quite old. I'll send you some screenshots of it after this call, that's easier than me explaining it.
Perfect. What do you need for the fund that you don't have?
Sorry, one second, someone's at my door. [pause] Okay, I'm back, sorry. Where were we?
The Julia story. It doesn't matter.
Right. What else about the employee affects the fund? Are they married, things like that?
And what are the options in that list?
Okay. Noted. Can I go back to source tax? You said all non-Swiss employees.
Sure, send it if it's easy. Do people need anything from you on the first day? Laptops, things like that? I just want to see if that belongs in the same form.
Okay. Anything else on who needs to do it? I'd rather hear all of it now.
Only the timing. When can we have this?
I'll come back to you on that this week, once we've gone through your screenshots.
Good. I'll send them after lunch. Thanks, Leo.

open_questions.question: What should be entered in the pension fund's 'Canton' field for employees living abroad, and does 'Canton' mean canton of residence or of work?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The field is required and lists only Swiss cantons; employees abroad are not asked for it (D-002), so their registration may be blocked.
options: Fund provides another value or procedure for residents abroad
'Canton' means work canton for everyone – then ask nobody and use the work canton
open_questions.recommendation: Keep D-002 (ask only residents of Switzerland); a domain expert verifies with Pensionskasse Muster.

open_questions.question: How does Pensionskasse Muster want registered partnerships and separated employees registered (its list has only Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed), and does it want the partner's details?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A wrong mapping gives the fund wrong civil status and possibly unnecessary or missing partner data.
options: Registered partnership → Married with partner's date of birth; Separated → Married (current provisional mapping)
Other mapping given by the fund
open_questions.recommendation: Keep the provisional mapping of D-003; verify with a domain expert and the fund.

open_questions.question: Does the fund's screen require the spouse's (or former spouse's) date of birth or other fields for Divorced or Widowed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The screenshots only show Single and Married; a hidden required field would block registration.
options: Extra field required – add a question
open_questions.recommendation: Domain expert obtains a screenshot of the fund screen for Divorced and Widowed.

open_questions.question: Does Lonio's computed tariff code match the Zurich calculator on the paths not explored: the residence block for A/B/H tariffs, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N, and the child rows marked inferred?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Lonio now owns the tariff result; unverified paths could produce wrong tariff codes.
options: Domain expert compares computed codes with the calculator before go-live
open_questions.recommendation: Go-live condition per D-009; non-blocking for the spec.

open_questions.question: Should the questionnaire ask for the nationality as a country, or only whether the employee (and the spouse) holds Swiss citizenship? And does the dual-citizenship rule (D-008) also apply to the spouse?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only 'Swiss or not' drives a rule; asking the full nationality may collect more than needed (G-01). The spouse's dual citizenship is not covered by D-008.
options: Ask the nationality as a country, Swiss citizens answer Switzerland (current model)
Ask 'Do you hold Swiss citizenship? yes/no' only
open_questions.recommendation: Keep the current model and confirm with the product owner; apply D-008 to the spouse unless a domain expert says otherwise.

questions.question: Which home address should the employee give: the current one, or the one that applies from the first working day? A new hire who is moving from abroad to Switzerland, or the other way, gets a different source tax liability, canton, cross-border questions and tariff code depending on which address counts. The spec treats the home address country as the country of residence without saying for which date.

Does the questionnaire start empty, or does it show the first working day HR already agreed, for the employee to confirm or correct? HR says 'I ask them to confirm it', which suggests HR already has a date. The spec only says the employee 'enters' it. This decides whether HR provides a value that is shown at the start.

Should the employee ever see the derived results (insurance start date, civil status as the fund will receive it, whether they are subject to source tax, the tariff code or the Liechtenstein result), for example before submitting or in the read-only view? Or are these recorded only for HR? The spec says 'recorded for HR' but never says what the employee sees.

For Liechtenstein residents with more than 45 non-return days, the calculator gives the normal tariff code together with 'Unter Vorbehalt des Doppelbesteuerungsabkommens' (subject to the double taxation agreement) (F-zh_source_tax_calculator-ab4e1e, C1Y / Unter Vorbehalt…). The spec records only the normal tariff code and flags only the 'no liability' case. Should the 'subject to the double taxation agreement' note and the HR flag also go with the tariff code in this case?

Liechtenstein residents who return daily, or expect at most 45 non-return days, get no tariff code. Yet they are asked the denomination, whether the spouse works, and all the children questions before the cross-border step, and none of those answers is used. Is that intended, given data minimisation (G-01)? Or should the cross-border questions come first for Liechtenstein residents so the tariff questions can be skipped, and should those answers be discarded on submission?

Child result row 22, and AC-06.4.3 with it: a minor child of a non-married employee who does NOT live in the household (parental custody, alternating care, employee pays more) 'counts with H'. The calculator note F-zh_source_tax_calculator-96658b says a child counts with H only when it lives in the household. Which is right: H or counted without H (A)? The answer changes the tariff letter.

The house number is required for every employee, but the notes say the sources do not cover addresses without one (rural addresses, building names, some foreign addresses). Can the employee submit without a house number, and if so how? As written, these employees cannot submit at all.

If the employee answers 'yes' to having children, must they add at least one child block before they can submit? And is there a maximum number of children? Today an employee could say 'yes' and add no child at all.

D-036 says inapplicable answers 'may be kept' until submission. AC-08.2.1 says they are kept and reappear when the earlier answer is changed back. Is keeping them a requirement or only allowed? Does it also apply if the employee leaves and comes back later in a new session, before submitting?

What are the valid ranges for dates? For example: can the first working day be in the past or far in the future, and must the date of birth (employee and spouse) be in the past or show a minimum age? Without this there are no rejection criteria to test.
The 60-day (Germany) and 45-day (Liechtenstein) questions refer to the calendar year. For someone who starts mid-year, does the employee estimate for the rest of the current year or for a full year?

Which countries can be chosen for the home address, the nationality and the spouse's residence and nationality? Is there an option for stateless people or an unknown nationality? And which of several non-Swiss nationalities should the employee enter?

Some example tables use the same item as both input and expected output (AC-08.4.2 lists 'Nationality' twice; AC-05.4.3 has 'Spouse / partner is gainfully employed…' as input and output 'asked'). Which value is the expected result, so the examples can be tested?

tech_leaks.quote: Step 7 'Children' – one block per child, repeated for each child the employee adds; all child_* conditions refer to the same child.
tech_leaks.why: 'child_*' is an internal field-id prefix used in prose. Business readers should not see identifier naming.

tech_leaks.quote: Afterwards Step 9 'Finish': permit reminder (rule permit_reminder), then submission
tech_leaks.why: Uses an internal rule id ('permit_reminder') in prose instead of the business name of the rule.

tech_leaks.quote: When Lonio has decided whether the employee is subject to source tax (rule subject_to_source_tax)
tech_leaks.why: Uses an internal rule identifier in an acceptance criterion. That is an implementation artifact, not business language.

tech_leaks.quote: (The formal expression covers one child block; the digit is the sum over all children.)
tech_leaks.why: Refers to how the rule is encoded (a 'formal expression' per child block). That is an implementation detail of the rule engine, not a business statement.

tech_leaks.quote: the employee goes through one block of questions per child and can add another child or remove one
tech_leaks.why: Prescribes the interaction (repeatable blocks with add and remove controls, copied from the calculator UI). The need is only to capture each child's answers.

tech_leaks.quote: their answers are kept, so that if the employee changes the earlier answer back, the earlier input reappears and need not be entered again
tech_leaks.why: Turns D-036's permissive 'may be kept' into required draft-retention and re-display behaviour, which is an implementation choice.

review.summary: Buildable: no errors, all 188 spec examples pass, all 5 open questions are non-blocking and no dev refinement question is a blocker. Before build, the product owner must decide 7 major dev refinement questions that change the tariff code, who is subject to source tax, or whether an employee can submit. The main one is the H-vs-A conflict on child row 22. Six technical leaks need wording fixes; some trace links are missing, and 8 items are inferred and need confirmation.

findings.title: Child row 22 contradicts the calculator: H or counted without H (A)?
findings.why: For a non-married employee's minor child who does not live in the household, the spec gives letter H. The calculator note says H applies only when the child lives in the household. This changes the tariff letter. The examples pass only because they test what the spec says.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement (major) on feature.md; AC-06.4.3; F-zh_source_tax_calculator-96658b; several AC-06.4.x/06.5.x examples marked '(to be verified)'; OQ-calculator-coverage
findings.action: Add a decision to decisions.yaml: row 22 gives 'counted without H' unless a domain expert confirms H with a calculator run. Fix AC-06.4.3 to match.

findings.title: Address reference date not defined
findings.why: For someone moving into or out of Switzerland, the address country decides whether they are subject to source tax, the canton, the cross-border questions and the tariff. The spec doesn't say whether the current address or the address from the first working day counts.
findings.action: Decide in decisions.yaml which address counts (recommended: the address from the first working day). Reword the home address question to match.

findings.title: Liechtenstein, more than 45 non-return days: double taxation note is missing
findings.why: The calculator returns the normal tariff code plus 'Unter Vorbehalt des Doppelbesteuerungsabkommens' (subject to the double taxation agreement). The spec records only the code, so HR loses this reservation.
findings.action: Decide that the tariff code is recorded together with the reservation note and an HR flag. Add an acceptance criterion to US-07.3/US-05.7.

findings.title: Required house number blocks some employees from submitting
findings.why: Addresses without a house number (rural addresses, building names, some foreign addresses) can't be submitted as written.
findings.action: Decide that the house number is optional, or allow an explicit 'no house number' choice. Update US-01.2.

findings.title: Liechtenstein residents are asked tariff questions whose answers are never used
findings.why: Residents who return daily, or have at most 45 non-return days, get no tariff code. They still answer the denomination, spouse and children questions, which goes against data minimisation (G-01).
findings.evidence: dev_refinement (major) on feature.md; G-01; US-08.4 step order (inferred, no cited fact)
findings.action: Decide whether the cross-border step comes first for Liechtenstein residents. Otherwise discard these answers on submission (extend D-036). Update the step order in US-08.4.

findings.title: Unclear who provides the first working day and what the employee sees
findings.why: HR says 'I ask them to confirm it', so a date set in advance by HR is likely. It is also undefined whether the employee sees derived results (insurance start date, fund civil status, tariff code). Both change the UI and the data flow.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement (major) on US-02.1 and US-05.7; trace_judge item.first_working_day (D-034)
findings.action: Add two decisions: (a) the date HR enters is shown at the start for the employee to confirm, or the employee enters it; (b) derived results are only for HR, or are shown to the employee before submitting.

findings.title: Technical leaks in the spec
findings.why: The text shows internal ids, rule-engine wording and interaction choices. Building them in limits engineering, and business readers can't follow the ids.
findings.evidence: tech_leak: feature.md ('child_*', 'rule permit_reminder', 'formal expression'); US-06.1 ('rule subject_to_source_tax', add/remove child blocks); US-08.2 (D-036 'may be kept' turned into a required re-display)
findings.action: Replace the ids with business names. State the need behind the child blocks ('capture answers for each child'). Reword AC-08.2.1 to match D-036 ('may be kept'), or record a decision that keeping them is required.

findings.title: Traceability gaps: claims or rows cite facts outside the cited set
findings.why: Unbacked statements weaken the cited knowledge model and can hide errors.
findings.evidence: trace_judge: 'H tariff' purpose on 8 child_* items; rows citing F-zh-52b67a, F-hr-b6d9b3, F-zh-e80d8f/ab4e1e (cross_border_tariff_applies, liechtenstein_no_source_tax_in_principle, source_tax_result); F-hr-d7431e (US-01.2, US-05.4); US-03.4 tariff letters; US-08.3 'date often moves'; US-08.4 nine-step order; item.address_country (D-010/D-038 not cited); fact_judge: F-zh-3058a4 garbled statement
findings.action: Add the missing fact or decision citations. Fix or remove the unbacked claims (for example, cite a fact for the H tariff purpose). Rewrite fact F-zh-3058a4.

findings.title: Non-blocking open questions and inferred items need sign-off before go-live
findings.why: The fund mapping, the canton for residents abroad and unverified calculator paths could produce wrong registrations or tariff codes.
findings.evidence: OQ-canton-abroad, OQ-civil-status-partnership, OQ-spouse-dob-other-status, OQ-calculator-coverage (D-009 go-live condition), OQ-nationality-wording; inferred: spouse_residence_country, spouse_nationality, child_tariff_result, US-04.2, US-06.3–06.5, US-08.4
findings.action: Assign a domain expert to check with Pensionskasse Muster and the Zurich calculator. Record the outcomes in decisions.yaml and mark the inferred items as confirmed.

findings.title: Smaller refinement gaps
findings.why: Without these there are no tests for rejected input, and some examples can't be tested as written.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement (minor): same item used as input and output (AC-08.4.2, AC-05.4.3); valid date ranges; 'has children = yes' with no child added, and a maximum number of children; mid-year estimate for the 60/45-day questions; country list, stateless people, several nationalities
findings.action: Fix the example tables. Add decisions on date ranges, at least one child when the answer is yes, the year basis for the day counts and the country list.
